The Wall Street Journal reported that Apple has been pursuing content deals worth up to nine figures, hoping to enhance Siri's AI access to the latest news and information. Details below.

Apple Seeks Publisher Deals for Siri AI

The Wall Street Journal reported today that Apple has been reaching out to various publishers, hoping to secure multi-year contracts that would allow Siri AI to access current events and information.

Details from the report:

Apple's move comes at a time when publishers are increasingly torn between taking AI companies to court or licensing content to them. For example, The New York Times is currently suing OpenAI and Microsoft over allegations of unauthorized use of its works to train AI models, but publishers including News Corp and IAC have chosen to strike content deals with the developer of ChatGPT.

Reddit has also pursued both strategies: in 2024, it struck a deal with Google (currently under review), reportedly worth around US$60 million per year, licensing its content for AI training; meanwhile, it has separately sued Anthropic and Perplexity, alleging they scraped its data without authorization.

Returning to the Wall Street Journal report, it noted that such deals are not new for Apple, as the company already partners with publishers on Apple News+ and has previously reached agreements including licensing publisher content for its own AI training.

The Wall Street Journal has reached out to Apple for comment, but Apple declined to comment.
